findings.impact: The result f34 required is now enforced: section 7 states the record obligation and item 19 places it inside the minimum set, so no completion gate can pass while a withdrawal lacks its reason. What is incomplete is the handoff and failure surface around that obligation. The withdrawal reason cannot originate inside Registry — Registry does not author why a release is withdrawn, and section 7 correctly refuses to let the Product Authorization decision's own reason code substitute — so it must arrive with the withdrawal command, yet the public port that section 8 enumerates declares only the decision ref. An implementer building the port signature from section 8, which is the contract's public-handoff surface, produces a withdrawal command with no reason parameter and satisfies section 8 completely, then fails item 19 at conformance. Section 10 leaves the same choice open: for the decision ref the contract distinguishes pre-mutation rejection from transaction rollback with two separate rows, while for the withdrawal reason item 19's "never commits without" does not say which applies, so an implementer must decide whether the reason is validated before mutation or enforced by rolling back the lifecycle transaction. The answer is readable — section 7 places the reason in the same lifecycle record as the decision ref, whose commit item 17 makes atomic — so this is a precision defect of the same class as the closed f31 rather than a missing rule, and it forces no redesign of the port, the record, or the enforcement boundary.
